commit.message:
Fix locations given to ident in `let%xyz ident in ..` (#5467)

This fixes a regression introduced in #5392, which adds the `let poly_`
syntax. Adding `poly_flag` to the let-pun case of `let_binding_body`
means `$loc` includes `poly_flag`, so `$loc($2)` should be passed to
`mkpatvar` and `ghexpvar` instead.

Unlike `rec` and `mutable`, the `poly_` flag is attached to idents
rather than let bindings. For example, `let%map poly_ x and poly_ y in ..`
is valid syntax, but `let%map rec x and rec y in ..` is not. Hence why
`poly_` is parsed in a differently from `rec` and `mutable`.

Refactor `Tpat_var` and `Tpat_alias` to use inline record types (#5437)

* Refactor Tpat_var and Tpat_alias to use inline record types

Convert Tpat_var and Tpat_alias pattern constructors from using multiple
tuple arguments to inline record types with named fields. This improves
code clarity and makes the constructor arguments more self-documenting.

Field names are prefixed (var_* and alias_*) to avoid OCaml's warning 30
about duplicate field names across different record types.

All usage sites across the codebase have been updated to use the new
record syntax, with punning applied where appropriate to reduce
verbosity.

commit.message:
chamelon: dune integration  (#5423)

chamelon: dune integration

This patch adds support for using `chamelon` directly on a dune project,
and integration in the Makefile with the `minimize-failure` and
`minimize-stdlib` targets (to minimize compilation failures in the
compiler/stdlib respectively).

The way the integration works is by parsing:

 - The output of `dune build --debug-dependency-path` to figure out the
   target containing a compilation error ;

 - The output of `dune show rules -r` to figure out the compilation
   commands to use to compile each of the targets

It then uses those rules to minimise the failing target and all its
dependencies within its dune executable/library.

Alternatively, if the failing target has already been determined
manually, the `--assume-failing` flag can be provided to skip the
detection of the failing target and directly start minimizing the
provided targets. In addition, `--extra-arg-for-failing-targets` can be
used to provide additional arguments to give to the compilation command
of the failing targets. This is useful e.g. to minimize error involving
certain specific types of invalids, passing `-dflambda` to the failing
target and an error (using `-e`) involving the given invalid.

In order to parse the S-expression output of `dune show rules`, this PR
integrates a copy of the lexer/parser from Sexplib, as well as the
printer from Sexplib0.

commit.message:
Remove support for thread-local dynamic bindings (#5171)

* Remove support for thread-local dynamic bindings

The dynamic variable semantics that our code expects is that [set_root] sets the
/global/ root, but the [set_root] implementation in the runtime sets the
per-thread root binding. The implementation of the Dynamic module in Basement[0]
just patches over this by maintaining its own root value per dynamic.

[0]: https://github.com/janestreet/basement/blob/with-extensions/src/dynamic.ml#L10-L13

We can save on a lot of complexity - and potentially even improve performance -
by just removing support for per-thread dynamic root bindings entirely. This
means that the API exposed by the runtime for dynamic bindings is basically just
[make], [get], and [with_temporarily]. Basement can continue to implement its
own mutable root binding semantics on top of this API, which is overall simpler
anyway.

* Update tests based on review

Ensure `requested_external_interrupt` is initialized before reading (#5424)

* Ensure requested_external_interrupt is initialized before reading

Fix a potential race in `caml_external_interrupt_all_signal_safe`, by making
sure that the `requested_external_interrupt` field is initialized *before*
`caml_external_interrupt_all_signal_safe` has a chance to write to it (it
doesn't write to it if `interrupt_word` is NULL, which gives us somewhere to
fence the store behind).

I have not observed this race happen in practice (it seems quite hard to
trigger; you'd need to be spawning a new domain at the same time
`caml_external_interrupt_all_signal_safe` is called); I just found it by reading
the code.

* Update runtime/domain.c

commit.message:
chamelon: add subcommands (#5421)

This patch adds subcommand support to the `chamelon` minimizer.
Currently, a single subcommand `run` is provided, with the same
interface as the existing `chamelon` binary. One should now use:

 $ chamelon run -c 'ocamlopt' file.ml

instead of

 $ # Old syntax, do not use!
 $ chamelon -c 'ocamlopt' file.ml

The old syntax is still supported with a warning nudging users to use
`chamelon run` instead.

This is the last step in preparation of the `chamelon dune` subcommand
to automatically minimize a complete `dune` library or executable
rather than an OCaml file (or set of OCaml files).

commit.message:
Add -dfexpr-annot flag to dump fexpr alongside cmx (#5210)

When `-dfexpr-annot` is provided, files `prog.raw.fl`,
`prog.simplify.fl` and `prog.reaper.fl` (if the reaper is enabled) are
produced alongside `prog.cmx` (similar to how a `prog.cmt` is produced
when `-bin-annot` is provided).

This provides a convenient way to dump the fexpr representation at
multiple stages of the pipeline into separate files by simply adding
`-dfexpr-annot` to the `ocamlopt_flags` (rather than having to parse
"After XXX:" headers from the standard output).

Note that compiling the compiler with `-dfexpr-annot` is currently
broken because of (many) missing primitives in the `fexpr`
printer/parser, but that is being worked on separately.

commit.message:
Indexing and arraylike primitives for small ints (#4779)

Small int arraylike primitives

Completes the array and indexing primitives for small integers. In
particular, for arrays, strings, bigstrings, and bytes support:
* storage of `int8`s, `int16#`s, and
* `int8#`, `int16#` indices.

New primitives for int8 and int16 need to be added because the upstream
primitives return zero-extended instead of sign-extended data.
```ocaml
external get8 : bytes -> int -> int = "%caml_bytes_get"
external get16 : bytes -> int -> int = "%caml_bytes_get16"
external geti8 : bytes -> int -> int8 = "%caml_bytes_geti8"
external geti16 : bytes -> int -> int16 = "%caml_bytes_geti16"
```
The `set16` primitives do not have this issue. Also, `set8` has been added
for naming consistency (along with `set8_indexed_by_*`, since `set_indexed_by_*`
primitives did not previously exist).

Tests

Non-SIMD tests have been added to
`testsuite/tests/typing-layouts/unboxed_int_stringlike_indexing.ml`, which is
generated by `generate_stringlike_indexing.ml`. (I also added a comment to the
former file noting that it is a generated test.)

SIMD tests have been added to `oxcaml/tests/simd/arrays*.ml`. These tests are
repetitive, but not generated.

Every new primitive has been added to a test, with the exception of the 512-bit
SIMD primitives. (No 512-bit tests existed before this patch.)

- Some (len, align) means safe with explicit length and alignment requirements

commit.message:
`int16` x86 intrinsics (#5407)

Int16 x86 intrinsics

Adds `caml_popcnt_int16`, `caml_lzcnt_int16`, and `caml_bmi_tzcnt_int16`
(see `backend/amd64/simd_selection.ml`). Basic tests are added to
`oxcaml/tests/simd/amd64/int_ops.ml`.

`simdgen` had to be extended to support instructions encoded with
multiple legacy prefixes. In particular, the operand-size override
prefix 0x66 needs to be emitted along with the prefix 0xF3 for the new
intrinsics.

To keep things simple, I added only an
`operand_size_override : bool` field to the `Legacy` constructor. This
means there are multiple ways to represent the 0x66 prefix, but the
binary emitter will always emit this prefix at most once.
`simdgen` will set `operand_size_override` if any of the `args`
registers is `R16`. With this rule, 4 instructions have
`operand_size_override` set: the 3 corresponding to the new intrinsics
and `crc32_r32_r16m16`, which is never used. (I'm not sure if this is
correct, but we can fix this when we expose an intrinsic for this
instruction)

commit.message:
chamelon: module minimization (#5356)

This patch changes the internal representation of chamelon minimizers
from minimizing "a set of files" to "a set of modules", where each
module contains both a `.ml` and a `.mli` file.

Most minimizers are adapted to work with this new representation with
minimal changes, since they are just applying a `Tast_mapper.mapper` on
the structure and can now transparently use the new
`tast_mapper_minimizer` helper.

Some minimizers (notably, the minimizers with multi-file support) still
use the same interface, and use the `multi_file_minimizer` helper which
converts from the new module-based representation to the legacy
file-based representation. These minimizers are thus currently unable to
minimize in interface files.

Merge missing upstream prerequisites for removing dynlink_compilerlibs (#5403)

* Replace structured constants by their Obj.t representation in CMO files

Before this commit, relocatable literals under the Reloc_literal
constructor were represented by objects
of type Lambda.structured_constant
in the CMO files. These objects were translated into their Obj.t
representation as they were loaded.

With this commit, the translation from Lambda.structured_constant
to Obj.t occurs as part of the compilation rather than when the CMO file
is loaded.

(cherry picked from commit 2cff470317783a1483c19abcba4a2de034b5845f)

This commit introduces the dedicated `compunit` (resp. `predef`) types to
represent names of compilation units (resp. predefined exceptions) in
CMO files. This makes the CMO format independent of the type checker's
 `Ident.t` type which, although it is domain-specific, can represent
identifiers which can actually not occur in CMO files, namely the
Local and Scoped categories of identifiers.

This commit also adds a `Global` module to `Symtable` to represent the
fact that, for the time being, the symbol table contains both
compilation units and predefined exceptions.

commit.message:
Bit matrix for interference graph (IRC) (#5296)

* Add BitMatrix alternative to PairSet for interference graph

Introduces RegisterStamp.BitMatrix as a memory-efficient alternative to
PairSet for storing interference graph edges. Uses a compact bit matrix
representation that stores only the upper triangle of the symmetric
adjacency matrix.

Key features:
- Same interface as PairSet for easy benchmarking
- Memory: O(n²/8) bytes vs hash table overhead
- Better cache locality for membership testing
- Trade-off: O(n²) cardinal/iter vs O(1)/O(edges) for PairSet

The bit matrix stores pairs (i,j) where i < j using the formula:
bit_offset = i * n - i*(i+1)/2 + (j-i-1)

Both implementations remain available for performance comparison.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Move cardinal and iter into For_debug submodules

Refactors PairSet and BitMatrix interfaces to nest cardinal and iter
operations within For_debug submodules, making it clear these operations
are for debugging/diagnostics rather than performance-critical paths.

Changes:
- PairSet.cardinal -> PairSet.For_debug.cardinal
- PairSet.iter -> PairSet.For_debug.iter
- BitMatrix.cardinal -> BitMatrix.For_debug.cardinal
- BitMatrix.iter -> BitMatrix.For_debug.iter

Updated all call sites in regalloc_interf_graph.ml and regalloc_irc.ml
to use the new paths. Both modules maintain identical interfaces for
easy interchangeability during benchmarking.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Define shared module type S for PairSet and BitMatrix

Introduces RegisterStamp.S module type to formalize the common interface
shared by PairSet and BitMatrix implementations. This ensures both edge
set implementations remain interchangeable and have identical signatures.

Changes:
- Added module type S within RegisterStamp module
- Declared PairSet : S and BitMatrix : S
- Simplified .mli by removing duplicate signature specifications

Benefits:
- Compiler enforces interface compatibility between implementations
- Makes interchangeability explicit for benchmarking
- Reduces code duplication in interface file
- Improves maintainability

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Use unsafe byte operations in BitMatrix for performance

Replaces safe Bytes.get_uint8 and Bytes.set_uint8 with unsafe versions
to eliminate bounds checking overhead in hot paths.

Changes:
- Added unsafe_get_uint8 external using %bytes_unsafe_get
- Added unsafe_set_uint8 external using %bytes_unsafe_set
- Replaced Bytes.get_uint8 with unsafe_get_uint8 in mem, add, and cardinal
- Replaced Bytes.set_uint8 with unsafe_set_uint8 in add

These operations are safe because:
- bit_offset calculation ensures indices are always within bounds
- The bytes array is sized exactly for the number of register pairs

Performance impact: Eliminates bounds checks on every edge membership
test and insertion, which are critical operations during register
allocation interference graph construction.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Factor out bit location computation in BitMatrix

Extracts the byte_index and bit_position calculation from a pair into
a dedicated bit_location function marked with [@inline always].

Changes:
- Added bit_location function that computes byte_index and bit_position
- Marked with [@inline always] to ensure inlining in hot paths
- Updated mem and add functions to use bit_location
- Reduces code duplication and improves maintainability

The inline always attribute ensures no performance regression from the
extraction, as the function will be inlined at all call sites.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Support self-loops in BitMatrix representation

Modified BitMatrix to store the diagonal, making it fully interchangeable
with PairSet. Previously BitMatrix rejected self-loops (i=i pairs) to save
space, but this created a behavioral difference from PairSet.

Changes:
- Include diagonal in storage: n*(n+1)/2 pairs instead of n*(n-1)/2
- Update bit_location formula: i*n - i*(i-1)/2 + (j-i)
- Remove i=j checks from mem and add functions
- Update For_debug.iter to include diagonal elements
- Add comment explaining the triangular storage layout

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Add random-based equivalence test for BitMatrix vs PairSet

This test verifies that BitMatrix and PairSet maintain identical behavior
across all operations using random testing. It exercises:

- Random add operations (including self-loops)
- Random membership queries
- Clear operations
- Cardinal computation
- Iteration order and completeness
- Comprehensive final check of all possible pairs

The test runs three scenarios with varying numbers of registers and
operations to ensure correctness across different scales. It successfully
caught an intentional bug where BitMatrix rejected self-loops while
PairSet accepted them.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Add BIT_MATRIX_THRESHOLD parameter for interference graph benchmarking

Add support for selecting between PairSet and BitMatrix representations
of the interference graph edge set via -regalloc-param BIT_MATRIX_THRESHOLD:k.

When num_registers < threshold, the BitMatrix representation is used.
Otherwise, the PairSet representation is used. Default threshold is 0,
so PairSet is used by default.

Changes:
- Add int_of_param to regalloc_utils for integer parameter parsing
- Introduce edge_set variant type in regalloc_interf_graph
- Add bit_matrix_threshold parameter (default: 0)
- Update graph operations to handle both representations
- Replace adj_set/cardinal with For_debug module
- Update callers in regalloc_irc and regalloc_irc_state

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Fix interference graph sizing to use Reg.For_testing.get_stamp()

Two critical bugs fixed:

1. Use Reg.For_testing.get_stamp() instead of list length
   Previously, make() used List.length (Reg.all_relocatable_regs())
   which doesn't account for:
   - Precolored registers with stamps
   - Potential gaps in stamp assignments
   This could cause out-of-bounds access in BitMatrix when a register
   with stamp >= allocated_size was encountered.

2. Handle register growth in clear()
   When reset calls clear, new registers may have been allocated since
   graph creation. The BitMatrix could be too small for the new stamp
   range. Solution:
   - Make adj_set mutable
   - Add capacity() to both PairSet and BitMatrix
   - In clear(), check if capacity < current stamp
   - Reallocate BitMatrix if needed (PairSet grows dynamically)

The reallocation in clear() is efficient: Bytes.make creates
zero-filled bytes without wasting time clearing old data.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Simplify PairSet to not track capacity

PairSet.capacity returns max_int since the hash table grows dynamically
and never needs reallocation. The capacity function only exists to satisfy
the module signature S, which BitMatrix needs to determine when to reallocate.

In practice, PairSet.capacity is never called - only BitMatrix.capacity
is checked in the clear() function.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Use bitwise operations in index computations

Bitwise operations, i.e. `land` instead of `mod` and `asr/lsr` instead
of '/', generate slightly shorter instruction sequences as they
produce different results, which does not matter in these cases, i.e.
the results are exactly the same for the all the values we are
interested in.

* Tweak documentation.

- Cardinal computation
- Iteration order and completeness
- Comprehensive final check of all possible pairs

The test runs three scenarios with varying numbers of registers and
operations to ensure correctness across different scales. It successfully
caught an intentional bug where BitMatrix rejected self-loops while
PairSet accepted them.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Add BIT_MATRIX_THRESHOLD parameter for interference graph benchmarking

Add support for selecting between PairSet and BitMatrix representations
of the interference graph edge set via -regalloc-param BIT_MATRIX_THRESHOLD:k.

When num_registers < threshold, the BitMatrix representation is used.
Otherwise, the PairSet representation is used. Default threshold is 0,
so PairSet is used by default.

Changes:
- Add int_of_param to regalloc_utils for integer parameter parsing
- Introduce edge_set variant type in regalloc_interf_graph
- Add bit_matrix_threshold parameter (default: 0)
- Update graph operations to handle both representations
- Replace adj_set/cardinal with For_debug module
- Update callers in regalloc_irc and regalloc_irc_state

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Fix interference graph sizing to use Reg.For_testing.get_stamp()

Two critical bugs fixed:

1. Use Reg.For_testing.get_stamp() instead of list length
   Previously, make() used List.length (Reg.all_relocatable_regs())
   which doesn't account for:
   - Precolored registers with stamps
   - Potential gaps in stamp assignments
   This could cause out-of-bounds access in BitMatrix when a register
   with stamp >= allocated_size was encountered.

2. Handle register growth in clear()
   When reset calls clear, new registers may have been allocated since
   graph creation. The BitMatrix could be too small for the new stamp
   range. Solution:
   - Make adj_set mutable
   - Add capacity() to both PairSet and BitMatrix
   - In clear(), check if capacity < current stamp
   - Reallocate BitMatrix if needed (PairSet grows dynamically)

The reallocation in clear() is efficient: Bytes.make creates
zero-filled bytes without wasting time clearing old data.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Simplify PairSet to not track capacity

PairSet.capacity returns max_int since the hash table grows dynamically
and never needs reallocation. The capacity function only exists to satisfy
the module signature S, which BitMatrix needs to determine when to reallocate.

In practice, PairSet.capacity is never called - only BitMatrix.capacity
is checked in the clear() function.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Use bitwise operations in index computations

Bitwise operations, i.e. `land` instead of `mod` and `asr/lsr` instead
of '/', generate slightly shorter instruction sequences as they
produce different results, which does not matter in these cases, i.e.
the results are exactly the same for the all the values we are
interested in.

commit.message:
Extract interference graph to dedicated module (IRC) (#5237)

* Extract interference graph to standalone module

This refactoring extracts interference graph functionality from the IRC
register allocator into a new reusable module regalloc_interf_graph.

Key changes:
- Created regalloc_interf_graph.ml/mli with graph type and operations
- Moved RegisterStamp and Degree modules from regalloc_irc_utils
- Replaced three state fields (adj_set, reg_interf, reg_degree) with
  single graph field in regalloc_irc_state
- Introduced callback-based filtering (iter_adjacent_if,
  for_all_adjacent_if) to avoid circular dependencies with IRC work
  list state
- All graph operations now delegate through the new module

Benefits:
- Clean separation of concerns (graph structure vs IRC algorithm)
- No circular dependencies
- Maintains dual representation (adj_set + adj_list) for performance
- Graph module could be reused by other allocators
- Same performance characteristics (inline functions preserved)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* `init_register_with_degree` -> `init_register_with_infinite_degree`

The only use case for `init_register_with_degree` seems to be to init
with `infinite` degree.

* Make `RegisterStamp.t` private and introduce `Pair` submodule

* Add `Reg.Stamp` module to abstract register stamps

This also then removes the `RegisterStamp` and `Pair` modules from the
graph module and renames the to `Edge`, which should be semantically
more precise.

This introduces some more type safety making it more difficult to
accidentally treat an arbitrary `int` as a register stamp.

* Rename internal `PS` to `EdgeTbl` for clarity

* Better description for the `Edge` module

* Consider packing register stamps for faster lookups

* Add Reg.Stamp.format function.

* simpler borrowing

Allow "borrow_" to be used as an attribute identifier by including

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Improve error reporting for explicit borrows in uniqueness analysis

Distinguish between implicit borrowing (closures) and explicit borrowing
(borrow_ keyword) by tracking lifted borrows separately. This produces
clearer error messages showing "borrowed" instead of generic "used" when
explicit borrows conflict with unique usage.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Remove boolean field from Pexp_borrow

- Change Pexp_borrow from 'expression * bool' to 'expression' in parsetree.mli
- Update all pattern matches across 8 files to remove boolean parameter
- Simplify and rename mark_borrow to is_borrow in typecore.ml
- Remove unused Borrow_out_of_context error from typecore.ml/mli
- Update borrow.ml test with new expected behavior

The boolean was a hacky mechanism to track whether a borrow had been
processed by the typechecker. Removing it makes the parsetree faithfully
represent user syntax. Borrows now naturally fail with mode errors when
used incorrectly rather than being artificially restricted by context checks.

* Add support for borrowing in quotations

This commit adds full support for the borrow_ syntax in quoted
expressions, allowing metaprogramming code to inspect and manipulate
borrowed expressions.

Changes:
- lambda/translquote.ml: Add Exp_desc.borrow to translate Texp_borrowed
- stdlib/camlinternalQuote.{ml,mli}: Add Borrow constructor and pretty-printer
- testsuite/tests/quotation/build_quotation.ml: Add tests for borrow_ in quotations

The borrow_ syntax is now preserved in quotations, e.g.:
  <[ let x = borrow_ 42 in x + 1 ]> -> <[let x = (borrow_ 42) in x + 1]>

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Track and validate borrowing contexts

Add tracking for borrowed expressions to ensure they are only used in
valid borrowing contexts (function arguments, let binding RHS, or
pattern match scrutinees). The borrow_ operator now carries a bool ref
that is marked true when used in a valid context during type checking.
The uniqueness analysis checks this flag and reports an error if a
borrowed expression is used out of context.

Changes:
- Modified Texp_borrowed to carry a bool ref tracking validity
- Added mark_borrowed_in_context function in typecore
- Updated borrowing contexts to mark borrowed expressions as valid
- Added Borrowed_out_of_context error in uniqueness_analysis
- Improved error message to explicitly list valid borrowing contexts
- Updated test expectations in borrow.ml

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Improve error message for borrowed values

Update error reporting to say "borrowed" instead of "used" when a value
is being borrowed. This makes error messages clearer by distinguishing
between regular usage and borrowing.

Example error message change:

  After:  "This value is used here as unique, but it has already been borrowed"

Update error message for `Lifted_borrowed` to explicitly mention that

This provides more context to users about why the borrowing prevents

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Previously, Usage.Borrowed fell through to the catch-all case and showed

A future improvement could find a better way to express the Borrowing

Refactor bigstring get/set safety properties (#5307)

* Refactor pbigstring_get/set_vec safety: use (len * align) option instead of unsafe bool

This refactors the safety checking for Pbigstring_load_vec and Pbigstring_set_vec
primitives to use a more explicit representation. Instead of a boolean 'unsafe'
flag, we now use 'safety : (len:int * align:int) option' where:
- None means unsafe (no bounds/alignment checks)
- Some (len, align) means safe with explicit length and alignment requirements

This allows for more precise control over safety checks in lambda_to_flambda_primitives,
where the access length and alignment can be specified independently rather than
being derived from the access_size type.
